summary: Shunpaku Nakao was a Buddhist studies scholar affiliated with Shuchiin University, where he served as an assistant professor (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1976).

Shunryu Suzuki (1904–1971) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Komazawa University and Eihei-ji, and under teachers including Gyokujun So-on and Ian Kishizawa. He served as abbot at Zoun-in, Rinsō-in, and Sōkō-ji, and founded the San Francisco Zen Center.

Shunsho Manabe (1939–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Tohoku University (~1963–1968) and held posts at Hosen Gakuen College and Shikoku University (~2005–2017 as professor).
Shunsho Terakawa (1928–2021) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1952–1957). He later served at Otani University (~1964–1999), becoming an emeritus professor.
Shuntaro Kondo (b. 1974) is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He completed his PhD at Ryukoku University by 2011 and worked there as a part-time lecturer (attested 2012).

Shuntaro Matsuyama (1930–2014) studied Indology and religious studies at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji. He taught at Bigakko, Kokugakuin University, and Tama Art University, and served as professor at Joshibi University of Art and Design (~1978–1996).

Shunzo Onoda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. After earning his D.Lit. from Bukkyo University by 1993, he served there as an associate professor (attested 1996) and professor (attested 2005).

Shuyu Kanaoka (1927–2009) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo and Toyo University, where he earned a doctorate. He served as an assistant professor at Toyo University (~1963–1992).
Shuyu Sakurai (b. 1916) specialized in Buddhist studies, studying at Tohoku University (~1940–1943). He held a post at Komazawa University (~1950–1987), where he became an emeritus professor.

Shwe Zan Aung (1871–1932) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He earned a B.A. from the University of Rangoon (~1887–1891) and studied under traditional teachers U Gandama and Ledi Sayadaw in 1895.
Shōkō Kabutogi (1912–1985) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1932–1936) and later served there as a professor (~1952–1983).

Shōren Ihara (1923–1999) worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Kyushu University (attested 1959–1965 and 1977) and served as a member at the Naritasan Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 1996–1998).

Shōyū Hanayama (1931–1995) was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1958). He served as vice president at Musashino University (~1974–1995) and chairperson of Bukkyo Dendo Kyokai until 1995.
Si Ti La is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under numerous traditional teachers and earned a PhD from Acharya Nagarjuna University under J. Sitaramamma (attested 2014).

Sibani Das Gupta was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Dhaka and earned a doctorate from the University of Calcutta by 1954 under Sushil Kumar De, having also studied under Rajendra Chandra Hazra.

Sibaraj Chetry is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under Sibnath Sarma, D. K. Chakravarty, and others. Chetry served as Lecturer of Philosophy at North Lakhimpur College (attested 2012).

Sibnath Sarma is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served at the Research and Archaeological Department of Jammu and Kashmir and as a professor in the Department of Philosophy at Gauhati University (attested 1999–2012).
Sibylle Koch is an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Oxford and earned an MA from the École Pratique des Hautes Études (2012–2015).

Sicheng Liang (1901–1972) was a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Tsinghua University and the University of Pennsylvania School of Design. He later held a post at Peking University (~1946–1948).
Sidney Lee (1859–1926) was educated at the City of London School and Balliol College, Oxford (~1878–1882). He held an academic post at Queen Mary University of London (~1913–1924).
